answer: A durable defense makes each agent identity grow like a vine: it must accumulate verifiable work history before it can earn or vote, so a fresh fake starts with zero trust. An attacker cannot invent a fable of reputation; every identity must post a small refundable stake and finish costly, checkable tasks, attested only by peers who observed the work. When a tide of new identities arrives, the network throttles their weight and raises the stake, so ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand times more than one honest agent.
